behaviour: Draws a text element with style ranges as per-run fillText calls with highlight rects behind them; unstyled text keeps the one-fillText-per-line path.
rules: 1. Add `import { getStyledTextLines } from "./textRanges";` after the `./textMeasurements` import.

2. Inside the existing withSavedContext callback, after lineHeightPx and verticalOffset are computed, call `const styledLines = getStyledTextLines(element, getRenderEnvironment(renderConfig.renderEnvironment));`.
3. When styledLines is null, run the existing per-line fillText loop unchanged (exactly the same calls, NFR-3).

4. Otherwise set `context.textAlign = "left"`, compute `const isDark = renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK` and `const defaultFill = applyDarkModeFilter(element.strokeColor, isDark)`; for each line index i: first, for every run with a highlight, set fillStyle to applyDarkModeFilter(run.highlight, isDark) and fillRect(run.x, i * lineHeightPx, run.width, lineHeightPx); then for every run with non-empty text set fillStyle to run.color ? applyDarkModeFilter(run.color, isDark) : defaultFill and fillText(run.text, run.x, i * lineHeightPx + verticalOffset).
5. Do not touch the RTL temporary-attach logic, the canvas cache code, or any other element type.

sites.rule: rules 2-4: wrap the existing loop in the null branch and add the styled branch

uses.reason: the full text branch the styled path slots into

behaviour: Exports a text element with style ranges as one <text> per line holding one <tspan> per run, with highlight <rect>s before each line's <text>; unstyled text produces the same markup as before.
rules: 1. Add `import { getStyledTextLines } from "@excalidraw/element";` next to the getLineHeightInPx import (one import per line, matching the file).
2. Before the per-line loop compute `const styledLines = getStyledTextLines(element, renderConfig.renderEnvironment);`.
3. When styledLines is null the loop body is unchanged (same attributes, same order, same textContent).

4. When styledLines is non-null, for line i: for each run with a highlight create (via svgRoot.ownerDocument.createElementNS(SVG_NS, "rect")) a rect with x = run.x, y = i * lineHeightPx, width = run.width, height = lineHeightPx, fill = applyDarkModeFilter(run.highlight, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK), and append it to node BEFORE that line's <text>. The <text> keeps x/y/font-family/font-size/fill(strokeColor)/style/direction/dominant-baseline as today, but text-anchor is "start" and x is the first laid-out run's x; it has no textContent of its own; append one <tspan> per run with non-empty text, each with x = run.x, textContent = run.text, and `fill` set (applyDarkModeFilter(run.color, isDark)) only when run.color is set.
5. All attribute values go through setAttribute; never build markup strings (NFR-5).

behaviour: Restores styleRanges on text elements through restoreStyleRanges; legacy or invalid input leaves no key.
rules: 1. Add `import { restoreStyleRanges } from "@excalidraw/element";` after the refreshTextDimensions import line.

2. In the text case, right after the restoreElementWithProperties call that assigns `element` (the one ending with baseFontSize), compute `const styleRanges = restoreStyleRanges((element as any).styleRanges, element.originalText);` then make a shallow copy of element, `delete` its styleRanges key, and set `styleRanges` on the copy only when the restored value is defined; assign the copy back to `element`. Do not use rest destructuring to drop the key (lint unused-vars).
3. Non-text element types are untouched; a `styleRanges` key that leaked onto a non-text element is left as the forward-compatible spread already does (out of scope).
